We need to fix execution errors. The error is about JUnit version mismatch: OutputDirectoryCreator not available. Usually caused by mixing JUnit 5 (junit-jupiter) with older platform engine. In our code, we have imports from JUnit Jupiter, but maybe the project dependencies are mismatched. However we cannot modify dependencies; we need to adjust test class to use JUnit 4 style? The platform expects test class naming pattern: default includes classes that start or end with Test. Our class is Message_findRRset_2_Test, which matches. The error is about engine versions, not test discovery.

Maybe the issue is that the test class is in package org.xbill.DNS, which is same as library code. That may cause classpath conflicts with JUnit? Not likely.

But typical fix: remove usage of @ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class) and Mockito static imports? Not causing engine mismatch.

The error mentions OutputDirectoryCreator not available; probably because JUnit Platform Launcher version mismatched with JUnit Jupiter Engine version. In this environment, we cannot change dependencies. Perhaps the test runner expects JUnit 4 tests; using JUnit 5 fails due to missing engine. So we could rewrite tests using JUnit 4 annotations (org.junit.Test, etc.) and remove JUnit 5 imports. That would allow the JUnit 4 engine (which is probably present). The test runner may default to JUnit 4. The error arises when trying to load Jupiter engine but missing OutputDirectoryCreator class (which is part of junit-platform-engine). So we should avoid JUnit Jupiter.

Thus convert to JUnit 4.

Also need to adjust parameterized test: use JUnitParams or JUnit 4 Parameterized? Simpler: replace edge type test with multiple @Test methods or loop.

Simplify: remove @ParameterizedTest, @MethodSource, and just test a few edge values manually.

Also remove @ExtendWith, MockitoExtension, and Mockito usage (the short-circuit test is commented out anyway). So we can remove Mockito imports.

The test class will use JUnit 4: import org.junit.*; static org.junit.Assert.*; Use @Before, @After, @Test.

Also need to handle expected exception: use @Test(expected = NullPointerException.class).
